solo.intro: Practice on your own: no clock, and as many tasks as you like.

_designNotes.buildState: Rooms, graph and scene specs written by _scratch/build_scenario.py (2026-11-06): the graded pair's Rothamsted world (cellars + glasshouses) the following summer at harvest, the home farm east of the walled garden. The stack yard hub (the wagon = deliver, Fisher's board = instrument, the notice board's two plaques link to the pair), pot_yard (L1, through the fence gate), barn (L2), field_edge (L3, out along the field track). Live scenario: class tasks are dealt by the live-class server (authoring_v2/live_class/pool/harvest.json) and never stored here; the book's practice pool is solo/pool.json. No codec id, no escape, ungraded. Music: chosen at closeout (a bright period track for Lucas to audition). Art: every room draws from text + skeleton.

worldPlatePrompt: One continuous single-frame view on a clear, warm late-summer afternoon from a little above the stack yard of an English experimental farm at harvest in the late nineteen-twenties: tall thatched corn ricks on a gravel yard, a blue-painted farm wagon with red wheels half loaded with golden wheat sheaves, a great tarred timber barn with its doors open, beyond a low fence a small yard of pot-grown wheat at the end of a long range of white-painted glasshouses, the high red-brick wall of a manor's walled garden with the manor's steep tiled roofs and tall chimneys over it, and a farm track running out between green hedges to fields of pale stubble with rows of stooks. Bright golden sunlight from the south-west, a deep blue sky. Photorealistic. No people, no animals, no text, nothing modern.
coverPrompt: Minimalist stylised thumbnail poster: the bold silhouette of a farm harvest wagon piled high with wheat sheaves, beside a single tall thatched rick, against a warm low sun. One bold, simple, high-contrast silhouette that reads at thumbnail size; flat limited palette of deep blue sky, dark silhouette and one warm amber glow of the sun. Strong negative space, soft film grain. Square. No people, no text.
story: It is harvest at the experimental station, the summer after the November fog, and the trial plots are being cut, weighed and carted home to the stack yard. Take a task at the pot bench in the pot-culture yard (one sheaf), the sheaf scale in the barn (two) or the stooks in the far field (three), run the analysis of variance in R, and choose your answer to fill the sheaves you carry. Bring each load back to the wagon and pitch it aboard: the trial's numbers are engineered for this class, but every analysis is the real one.

rooms.title: The stack yard
rooms.designNote: HUB. The harvest wagon is the deliver point (carry-back: sheaves count only once pitched aboard); Fisher's board is the read-by-eye instrument (kind anova_board, the copied demonstration config, never class data). The notice board's two notices link to the graded pair (plaque `link`, hidden in a live class session). Doors: the brick-piered gateway to the pot-culture yard (L1), the barn's great doors (L2), the gap in the far fence onto the field track (L3, the furthest).
